question: Birjis Qadr, the son of the deposed Nawab Wajid Ali Shah, was proclaimed the new Nawab of a princely state in which place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Birjis Qadr** was the son of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah, the last ruler of the princely state of Awadh (Oudh).
 
• In 1857, during the Indian Rebellion (First War of Independence), Birjis Qadr was **proclaimed the Nawab of Lucknow** by the rebels.
 
• His ascension was supported by his mother, **Begum Hazrat Mahal**, a prominent leader of the rebellion in Awadh.
 
• Lucknow became a significant center of resistance against British rule during the revolt, with the rebels fighting to restore the sovereignty of the Nawabs of Awadh.
 
• Despite initial successes, the British forces recaptured Lucknow in March 1858, forcing Birjis Qadr and Begum Hazrat Mahal into exile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wajid Ali Shah:**

 
 
• The last Nawab of Awadh, he was deposed by the British in 1856 on charges of misgovernance.
 
• He was exiled to Calcutta (now Kolkata) after the annexation of Awadh.
 
• Wajid Ali Shah was also a patron of arts, known for his contributions to music, dance, and poetry.
 
 
 
• **Begum Hazrat Mahal:**
 
 
• The wife of Wajid Ali Shah and mother of Birjis Qadr, she played a crucial role in the 1857 rebellion.
 
• She led the resistance against the British in Awadh, rallying support from various sections of society.
 
• After the fall of Lucknow, she fled to Nepal, where she lived in exile until her death.
 
 
 
• **The Annexation of Awadh:**
 
 
• In 1856, the British East India Company annexed Awadh under the pretext of "misgovernance" using the Doctrine of Lapse.
 
• The annexation caused widespread discontent among the local population, contributing to the 1857 rebellion.
 
 
 
• **The Indian Rebellion of 1857:**
 
 
• Also known as the First War of Independence, it was a major uprising against British rule in India.
 
• It began with the sepoys (Indian soldiers in the British army) and later gained support from various princely states and civilians.
 
• The rebellion was eventually suppressed by the British, but it marked the beginning of organized resistance against colonial rule.
